author: Sohail Aziz
attribution: Photo: Sohail Aziz, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Sign_Board_of_Golra_Sharif_Railway_Station.jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Hand-painted station name board, frontal. Urdu has ڑ (clear small ط above) and ends in a round isolated heh, transcribed as Urdu ہ. 'JN' is small and underlined with two dots under it (abbreviation mark). The prime after 1994 is painted as a small tick above the 4.
source_title: File:Sign Board of Golra Sharif Railway Station.jpg
source_categories: Bilingual train station name signs in Pakistan

attribution: Photo: *_*, CC BY 2.0, via Flickr. Source: https://www.flickr.com/photos/22539273@N00/15666918956. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Long printed banner of animal photos over a green canopy at the zoo entrance, seen from below at a strong angle; letters are large and clear.

author: Martha C.
attribution: Photo: Martha C., Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Sign_for_foreigners_Karakoram_Highway_Sep_2004.jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Overhead blue Karakoram Highway (N-35) gantry with three panels, Latin + Chinese + Cyrillic (for foreign travellers). Cyrillic is as painted: 'СУАТ' with odd letter heights and 'ХУНЗРЕАб' with a lowercase б. The Chinese lines (2-4 characters each, some apparently malformed) are NOT transcribed. A tour bus with its number plate and tourists stand below the sign (incidental, seen mostly from behind).
source_title: File:Sign for foreigners Karakoram Highway Sep 2004.jpg
source_categories: Signs on Karakoram Highway in Pakistan

author: Jugni
attribution: Photo: Jugni, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Nando%27s_at_MM_Alam_Road.jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Free-standing yellow/green board with the rooster logo outside Nando's, M.M. Alam Road, Gulberg, Lahore; slightly angled. The apostrophe in Nando's is a curly typographic quote on the sign.

author: Khadija tauqir123
attribution: Photo: Khadija tauqir123, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Pakistani_culture.jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Roadside restaurant (Khyber Pakhtunkhwa) seen far across a wheat field, signs small in frame. Labelled: the billboard name (پاچادربار, written without a space) and the painted wall text 'PACHA DARBAR / Restaurant'. Not transcribed: the billboard's second word (probably ریسٹورنٹ) and phone numbers, too small to read with certainty; the large yellow wall lettering repeats پاچادربا... and is cut off by hay bales. Pepsi logos and a decorated truck are distractors.

author: Danish47
attribution: Photo: Danish47, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Road_sign_in_Islamabad.JPG. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Advance direction sign for Faizabad Interchange, Islamabad. Urdu uses ہ (لاہور), ٹ (ائیرپورٹ) and ڈ (راولپنڈی). Urdu top line reads right to left 'ائیرپورٹ ... لاہور' with a wide gap; the airport word is written ا-ئ-ی-ر (hamza on the second tooth). Space before the comma in 'Lahore , Airport' is on the sign. Airplane pictogram and N-5 hexagon.

author: Omar Usman Khan
attribution: Photo: Omar Usman Khan, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Signboard_of_Syed_Ahmad_Shaheed.jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/. Unmodified original.

lines.latin: Mazar Sayyid Ahmad Shahid (Shrine of Syed Ahmad Shaheed)

notes: Hand-painted calligraphic name board of the Syed Ahmad Shaheed shrine (Balakot/Mansehra). The mark over سید is read as a shadda. شہید is transcribed with Urdu ہ (the calligraphic medial heh could also be read as ھ). The small yellow honorific at top left (رحمۃ اللہ علیہ) and the two small blue lines below (dated 6 مئی 1831) are not transcribed. Worker with wheelbarrow incidental.
source_categories: Tomb of Hazrat Shaheed Ahmad Maujadid Baralvi, Mansehra

author: Fazalrahimawan
attribution: Photo: Fazalrahimawan, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Sign_Board_-_Jinnan_Wali_Dheri.jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Faded blue archaeology direction sign (left arrow) at a roadside, mid-distance; paint chipped. Urdu ڈھ (ڈ + do-chashmi ھ) and noon ghunna ں in جنوں (no dot visible); the worn Urdu should be checked. English spelled 'JINAH' on the sign. Distractor: Sarhad Rural Support Programme board with 'KH 15' graffiti at left.

author: Khalid Mahmood
attribution: Photo: Khalid Mahmood, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Road_sign_Islamabad_(cropped).JPG. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Stack of four direction signs in Islamabad, all pointing left. Urdu uses ہ in سوہاوہ and کوہ; no visible gap between پیر and سوہاوہ (ر does not join). On the 7th Avenue panel the Urdu has one more glyph right of ایونیو, an angled stroke with a long base that is probably the Urdu digit ۷ in a Nastaliq style (or ے); it is left out of the label because it cannot be read with certainty.

author: Kash_if
attribution: Photo: Kash_if, CC BY 2.0, via Flickr. Source: https://www.flickr.com/photos/79406424@N00/2487856374. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Two right-pointing direction signs in Islamabad, close-up and tilted about 15 degrees; airplane pictogram on the blue panel. Urdu ٹ in both words; زیروپوائنٹ written without a space. The cut-off green 'Mot...' (Motorway) panel at the top and a decorated truck at bottom right are distractors.

author: کراچی
attribution: Photo: کراچی, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Flickr. Source: https://www.flickr.com/photos/13597223@N02/8620097398. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Weathered painted board on a school-side shop, Karachi; red 'SCHOOL UNIFORMS' is faded. Small 'TIME MON TO SAT 8AM TO 6PM' panel and the Pakola logo at top right are not labelled. The neighbouring 'INSIDE SCHOOL' board with a small Urdu line (apparently 'اسکول کے اندر', not verified letter by letter) is a distractor. The person lying on the pavement is incidental, face not visible.
source_title: Gulistan Shah Abdul Lateef Bhittai Primary School IMG-20130404-00475

author: Inam Photography
attribution: Photo: Inam Photography, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Flickr. Source: https://www.flickr.com/photos/60263060@N07/11410992273. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.0/. Unmodified original.

lines.text: امپورٹڈ سائیکل کی تمام ورائٹی ہول سیل
lines.latin: Imported cycle ki tamam variety, wholesale (all varieties of imported bicycles, wholesale)

notes: White shop board of Kausar Cycle Store at Chowk Neela Gumbad, Lahore, below the blue-tiled dome; power lines cross the board. Urdu ٹ in سٹور and ورائٹی, ڈ in امپورٹڈ. A fourth tiny line (about rates and discounts) is not transcribed. Distractors: PHOENIX / AHMAD TRADERS and STAR CYCLE WORKS boards (Latin, with Lahore addresses) below and beside it. Small 'INAM Photography' photographer mark at bottom right (not across the image).

'SHAFIQUE AUTOS WORKSHOP' board on the pole and Urdu van lettering are distractors. location is where the photo was taken (Commons camera coordinates), not the target.

notes: Rooftop board of a travel agency in Lahore, crossed by power lines. Not transcribed: the tiny tagline above the name, the licence numbers under it, the partly hidden word left of the plane, the route line (Lahore - Jeddah - Madina - Lahore), and phone numbers that are partly hidden by cables. The vertical 'RAINBOW TRAVELS' blade sign below repeats the name. location is where the photo was taken (Commons camera coordinates), not the target.
